speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We take them into consideration in our periodic reviews of the design and implementation of the scheme, as well as guidelines and advice given to the CHAS clinics.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I promised my resident that I would raise this.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I have to convey this unhappy feedback, mostly from the Orange cardholders.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The unhappy part about it is the $1,100 monthly household income cut-off criterion per person is too low to qualify for the Blue card.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given that the Orange card is so unpopular and not so appreciated, maybe we should just move more to the Blue card.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That will also take some of the patient load off the polyclinics because there are still a lot of people going to the polyclinics as it is a lot cheaper.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If we can expand this group, that is, to have more getting the Blue card, that would probably improve the well-being of everyone and also ease the workload at the polyclinics.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, I myself face certain suggestions and pressures from my own residents, too.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I mentioned in my reply, MOH takes feedback from patients, Singaporeans and also from GPs on the scheme.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: From the number of CHAS cards issued, what percentage of our population is covered?
